title.en: Planning and the goals of five year plans

hook.en: In 1950 India had to choose: leave the economy to the market, or let the government plan it? The leaders chose a mixed path. Why?
hook.kn: 1950ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತ ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯನ್ನು ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆಗೆ ಬಿಡಬೇಕೇ, ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಯೋಜಿಸಬೇಕೇ ಎಂದು ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಿತ್ತು. ನಾಯಕರು ಮಿಶ್ರ ಮಾರ್ಗ ಆರಿಸಿದರು. ಏಕೆ?

objectives.en: Explain the mixed economy chosen by India
Describe the Planning Commission and five year plans
State the four goals of planning

narration.en: In 1950 India had to choose: leave the economy to the market, or let the government plan it? The leaders chose a mixed path. Why?
narration.kn: 1950ರಲ್ಲಿ ಭಾರತ ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯನ್ನು ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆಗೆ ಬಿಡಬೇಕೇ, ಸರ್ಕಾರ ಯೋಜಿಸಬೇಕೇ ಎಂದು ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡಬೇಕಿತ್ತು. ನಾಯಕರು ಮಿಶ್ರ ಮಾರ್ಗ ಆರಿಸಿದರು. ಏಕೆ?

body.en: India chose a mixed economy, combining the best features of capitalism and socialism, with both a public and a private sector. The Planning Commission was set up in 1950 with the Prime Minister as its chairperson. Five year plans set targets; the First Five Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956. P.C. Mahalanobis, who guided the Second Plan, is called the architect of Indian planning.
body.kn: ಭಾರತ ಬಂಡವಾಳಶಾಹಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾಜವಾದದ ಉತ್ತಮ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿದ ಮಿಶ್ರ ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯನ್ನು ಆರಿಸಿತು. 1950ರಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಧಾನ ಮಂತ್ರಿ ಅಧ್ಯಕ್ಷತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯೋಜನಾ ಆಯೋಗ ಸ್ಥಾಪನೆಯಾಯಿತು. ಪಿ.ಸಿ. ಮಹಾಲನೋಬಿಸ್ ಭಾರತೀಯ ಯೋಜನೆಯ ಶಿಲ್ಪಿ.

title.en: On the board: Planning and its four goals

say.en: In 1950 India set up the Planning Commission, chaired by the Prime Minister.
The First Plan ran from 1951 to 1956. Mahalanobis, architect of planning, guided the Second.
The plans had four goals: growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity.
Growth is measured by the rise in GDP. From 200 to 212 lakh crore is 6 per cent.

title.en: Goals of the Five Year Plans

prompt.en: Sort each example under the planning goal it serves.
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಉದಾಹರಣೆಯನ್ನು ಅದು ಸಾಧಿಸುವ ಯೋಜನಾ ಗುರಿಯಡಿ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

text.en: A steady rise in the country's GDP
More output of goods and services every year
Farmers adopting new seed varieties and machines
Accepting that women have the same rights as men
Growing enough food grains at home instead of importing them
Avoiding imports of goods India can make itself
Land reforms that give land to the tiller
Making sure the benefits of growth reach the poor

explanation.en: The plans aimed at growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity. The goals could pull against each other, so each plan balanced them differently.

title.en: Four goals: growth, modernisation, self-reliance, equity

body.en: Growth means a steady increase in the country's GDP. Modernisation means adopting new technology and changing social outlook, such as recognising that women have the same rights as men. Self-reliance means avoiding imports of goods that can be produced at home, especially food. Equity means the benefits of growth should reach the poor.
body.kn: ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಜಿಡಿಪಿಯ ಸ್ಥಿರ ಏರಿಕೆ. ಆಧುನೀಕರಣ ಎಂದರೆ ಹೊಸ ತಂತ್ರಜ್ಞಾನ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಮಾಜಿಕ ದೃಷ್ಟಿಕೋನದ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ. ಸ್ವಾವಲಂಬನೆ ಎಂದರೆ ದೇಶದಲ್ಲೇ ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸಬಹುದಾದ ವಸ್ತುಗಳ ಆಮದು ತಪ್ಪಿಸುವುದು. ಸಮಾನತೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯ ಲಾಭ ಬಡವರಿಗೂ ತಲುಪುವುದು.

points.en: GDP growth needs more capital and efficient support services
Plans could not give equal weight to every goal at once
